title: Fix the quarantine reasons
prompt: The quarantine step should set aside every transaction that breaks a rule, with the first rule it breaks as `reason`. The audit found transactions without an account in the load, and some that reached neither table. Fix `solve(transactions)` so it returns the quarantined transactions.
rules: The rules are checked in the order of the list; the first one a transaction breaks is its `reason`.
A missing value breaks the rule that checks it: a missing amount is a `bad_amount`, a missing currency an `unknown_currency`.
Return `transaction_id`, `account_id`, `amount`, `currency` and `reason` for the quarantined transactions only.
hints: Run the starter on the sample. Which reasons ever come out? Look at what `reason` holds after the loop.
`reason = F.when(...)` inside the loop replaces the expression each time. Start the chain with the first rule and add `.when(...)` for each later one.
A rule on a missing value is NULL, and `F.when` skips NULL. Turn it into a failure with `F.coalesce(condition, F.lit(False))`.
explanation: The loop rebuilt `reason` from scratch on every pass, so only the last rule, `unknown_status`, ever labelled a row: a transaction without an account got no reason and went to the load. The fix starts the chain with the first rule and adds `.when(...)` for each later rule, so the first broken rule wins. The second bug is NULL: `amount > 0` on a missing amount is NULL, `F.when` treats that as not matched, and the row got no reason, so it was in neither table. `F.coalesce(condition, F.lit(False))` makes it count as broken. A quick check after the fix: the rows with a reason plus the rows without one add up to the whole feed.
